title: Add session workflow tools: end-session.sh, Deploy JFSN.command, CURRENT_STATE.md
body:
- end-session.sh: end-of-session ritual — checks uncommitted files,
  prompts for commit message, pushes, runs backup, reminds to update memory
- "Deploy JFSN.command": double-clickable Mac file, opens Terminal and
  runs end-session.sh. Put on Desktop or Dock.
- CURRENT_STATE.md: current project state, pending todos, known issues.
  Updated by end-session.sh on every run.

title: Theme repass complete: Mr. SNOWmann 791→72, Gallery 211→149
body:
Two full repasses using claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 with tightened
ai_notes. Key changes:

  figure is clearly visible. 791→72 works.

- Gallery: outdoor/street art excluded. 211→149.

title: Fix theme rules + add repass_themes.py
body:

was 'apply to ALL collages' (→ 791 wrongly tagged); Gallery was applying
to outdoor murals; Framed was matching rectangular packaging. Each rule
now requires the theme to be clearly visible and primary.

title: Add client onboarding workflow + setup-client.sh
body:

delivery — intake checklist, email template, every command in order,
curation guide, quality checklist, deploy steps, adding works later,
pricing table, common problems.

setup-client.sh: one command to scaffold a clean client project from
the JFSN template. Copies code + scripts, excludes artwork images and
all Jeff-specific data, creates empty artworks/ dirs, inits fresh git.
Usage: bash setup-client.sh sarah-jones

title: Add The Companion — text prompt → matched archive works (#4 from wow backlog)
body:
New page companion.html: type a feeling, word, or memory → Claude Haiku
picks 1–3 real works from the catalog that resonate, with a sentence
about why each fits. Oracle-style UI, staggered fade-in results,
example chips, "Try another" reset.

Netlify function netlify/functions/companion.mjs keeps the API key
server-side. CORS-open so it works from jfsn.com (cPanel) in the
interim and from jfsn-archive.netlify.app natively. Samples 200 works
per query from catalog-lite for speed. Uses claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.

Also: "Companion" added to footer nav on all 12 pages; companion.html
added to sitemap in build_catalog.py.

in a masonry grid using the same CSS/span formula as archive.html.
Titles are editable inline (click the hover overlay). After all 10 are
placed, the drop zone collapses to a compact "add more" bar and locks

#demo so visitors can discover the feature without scrolling.

title: Dating pass complete: 100% coverage (1,084/1,084) + fix curate.html "Undated" filter
body:
The remaining 319 undated works have been assigned years through curate.html's
Years tab. Archive coverage is now 100%. The real fifty-year shape is finally
visible — including a confirmed lean period in the 1980s (only 11 works).

Final distribution by decade:
  1970s:  58   formative
  1980s:  11   sparse (real lean period)
  1990s: 193   productive
  2000s: 274   peak
  2010s: 307   peak
  2020s: 241   recent

11 same-or-different-decade conflicts preserved per apply_dates.py default
(existing sidecar year wins). Resolve case-by-case later if desired.

Also: curate.html "Undated" filter bug fix. The filter was using a broader
"untagged across all dimensions" predicate (no theme AND no year AND no
series), which showed 0 results because every work has at least one theme.
Now mode-aware: in years mode it filters works by `years[id] == null`; in
series mode by `seriesAssign[id] == null`; only themes mode keeps the
original "fully untagged" semantics.

title: Add /changes.html — a living changelog of the archive
body:
Parses git log at build time into changes.json and renders a newest-first
typographic feed. The archive is a living personal record, not a snapshot;
this page makes the ongoing work visible.

- artworks/build_changes.py: parses git log into changes.json. Strips
  Co-Authored-By trailers for a cleaner public feed. Invoked from
  build_catalog.py so every build refreshes the changelog.
- changes.html: feed page modeled on privacy.html typography. Dates
  rendered as "27 May 2026", short SHA shown, commit body preserved
  with pre-wrap formatting.
- Footer-nav: Changes link added across 12 pages (between For Artists
  and Privacy). Header nav kept lean.
- Sitemap: changes.html added.

title: Add time-machine scrubber to timeline.html
body:
A single chronological strip of all 765 dated works at the top of
timeline.html — the payoff for the dating pass earlier this session.
The natural density of the strip itself tells the fifty-year story:
sparse 1980s, dense 1990s and 2020s.

Mechanics:
- Decade marker buttons (1970s through 2020s) — click to jump-scroll
  the strip to the first thumb of that decade.
- Click-and-drag scrubbing on desktop (pointer events, with drag-vs-click
  distinction so dragging never opens an artwork).
- Native touch scroll on mobile.
- Active decade auto-highlights based on the thumb nearest the viewport
  center as the user scrolls.
- Defeats browser scroll-restoration so the strip always starts at 1970.
- Existing per-decade strips preserved below for focused browsing.

title: Dating pass: 653 newly dated works (10% → 70% coverage) + cold backup infra
body:
Adds apply_dates.py to push __years__ decisions from curate.html back to
sidecars and pending-themes.json (default preserves existing more-specific
year values; --overwrite required to replace). Adds backup.sh for incremental
cold backup of the full project to JEFFS-4TB via rsync, with write-probe
and file-count verification. Catalogs and api/v1/ rebuilt; all 6 decades
now populated (1970s:57, 1980s:11, 1990s:190, 2000s:131, 2010s:158, 2020s:218),
unblocking the time-machine scrubber for timeline.html.

Also commits accumulated post-launch work from prior sessions that was
deployed but never staged:
- lost.html: memorial page for the 500-1,000 works lost to water and bed bugs;
  linked from about.html.
- privacy.html: 8-section privacy notice (GoatCounter + Netlify Forms
  disclosure); linked from footer-nav across all public pages.
- for-artists.html funnel: Netlify inquiry form, tier-aware Inquire buttons,
  founding-artist 30% callout, Service JSON-LD with AggregateOffer × 3,
  8 FAQ entries, commented-in Testimonials section.
- XXXIII · Guernica series: 232 works curated.
- artist-config.json + artist-config.js: single source of truth for vocab.
- colors.json: dominant color per thumbnail.
- Site-wide: current-page nav indicator (aria-current orange underline),
  black-on-orange text contrast standardized, For Artists in header/footer
  nav on all pages, robots.txt sitemap URL typo fixed, sitemap.xml entries
  completed, sw.js cache key bumped.
